newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki rises on strong Kesko, Merita, Sentra.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki rises on strong Kesko, Merita, Sentra.

text.p: Shares rose on Monday to another new high on strong showings by wholesale and retail group Kesko, banking group Merita, and wholesaler Sentra, with a late boost coming from gains on Wall Street, brokers said.

The HEX index put on 0.56 percent to 2,821.91 but volume was slightly slower than recenely, totalling 600 million markka, and brokers said the mood fairly hesitant, with a raft of key corporate reports this week due to set the tone.
Kesko rose more than six percent, up 4.30 markka to 70.80, in heavy 50 million markka turnover after announcing a deal on Friday to sell parts of its Tuko unit to meet European competition demands.
Analysts said European Commission competition authorities are now likely to approve the changes to Kesko's purchase of its former rival.
Kesko said late on Friday it would sell parts of the Tuko operations it bought last May in a deal subsequently blocked as anti-competitive by the EU Commission.
"This is definitely good news for Kesko," said Merita Bank analyst Tanja Lounevirta. The plan would let Kesko keep two well-performing Tuko units, Anttila and Rautia.

Sentra rocketed more than 60 percent, gaining 100.00 markka to close at 260.00 in fair five million markka trade, boosted by Friday's news that it was buying part of Tuko, improving its earnings prospects.
Merita, which indirectly owns a majority stake in Sentra ended brisk trade 0.60 higher at 18.00 markka.
But Nokia slipped against the trend, ending down 1.20 markka at 322.00.
